derivations.claim: The monic relations make $\mathbb A$ free over $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb R$ free over $\mathbb Z[h]$, each with basis $1,X$. Both relations are homogeneous for the displayed degrees. For the odd maps, the merge quotient is well-defined because $p(C_1-C_2)=0$. The split formula is independent of whether $j(C)=C_1$ or $C_2$, since $(C_1-C_2)\wedge C_1=(C_1-C_2)\wedge C_2=C_1\wedge C_2$.

In $\mathbb R$, associativity, commutativity and the unit law follow from quotient-ring multiplication. On the basis $1,X$, the counit composites $(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta$ and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\epsilon)\Delta$ both send $1\mapsto1$ and $X\mapsto X$. Cocommutativity follows from the symmetric formulas for $\Delta(1)$ and $\Delta(X)$. For coassociativity, both iterated comultiplications send $X$ to $X\otimes X\otimes X$ and send $1$ to $1\otimes X\otimes X+X\otimes1\otimes X+X\otimes X\otimes1-h(1\otimes1\otimes X+1\otimes X\otimes1+X\otimes1\otimes1)+h^2 1\otimes1\otimes1.$ Thus the unit, counit and coassociativity axioms hold.

On the ordered basis $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$, each of $\Delta m$, $(m\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)$, and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes m)(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})$ has respective outputs $1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h1\otimes1,\quad X\otimes X,\quad X\otimes X,\quad hX\otimes X.$ Therefore the Frobenius identities hold. On every cube square, the two unsigned composites agree by tensor functoriality on disjoint circles, associativity for two merges, coassociativity for two splits, or the checked Frobenius identities for a merge-split pair. Opposite cube signs make the two signed composites cancel, so the Bar–Natan differential squares to zero. A based odd cube with the square-compatible sign data in [A1] is also a cochain complex: the coefficient of each height-two state in $d^2$ is the sum of its two signed composites, zero by the defining condition. The right marked action commutes with merges because the quotient carries $Z_p$ to the marked output circle. It commutes with splits because $((C_1-C_2)\wedge j(z))\wedge Z_p=(C_1-C_2)\wedge j(z\wedge Z_p)$, including a split of the marked circle: either lift of the marked output differs by $C_1-C_2$, whose extra wedge vanishes. Also $X^2$ acts by zero. Every state module is free over $\mathbb A$: choose the exterior products of unmarked circle generators as module basis and append $Z_p$ on the right for their $X$ multiples. Modulo $2$ this action is precisely the even marked action, and reduction of $\mathbb R$ modulo $(2,h)$ retains that action through $\mathbb B$, rather than setting $X=0$. Existence of such odd sign assignments, the mod-2 comparison as a homotopy equivalence, and the localized rank-one condition are not claimed by this Definition; they are separate assertions of the foundations lemma. Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. A **cochain complex in $\mathcal A$**
is a family of objects $(C^n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ together with morphisms
$$d^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$$
such that
$$d^{n+1}\circ d^n=0$$
for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

This page uses the reindexing convention that a cochain complex $C^\bullet$ may
also be read as the chain complex with $(C^\sharp)_n:=C^{-n}$ and
$d^\sharp_n:=d^{-n}$, so that lower and upper indices differ only by the sign
of the grading.

derivations.claim: The quotient $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$ has basis $1,X$, and its multiplication table is the displayed $m_L$. Hence multiplication is associative and commutative with unit $1$. The counit identities follow on $1,X$: $(\epsilon_L\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta_L(1)=1$, $(\epsilon_L\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta_L(X)=X$, and the other counit composite gives the same values.

For input $1$, both composites $(\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta_L$ and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta_L)\Delta_L$ equal $1\otimes X\otimes X+X\otimes1\otimes X+1\otimes1\otimes1+X\otimes X\otimes1$. For input $X$, both equal $1\otimes1\otimes X+1\otimes X\otimes1+X\otimes1\otimes1+X\otimes X\otimes X$. Thus $\Delta_L$ is coassociative. Cocommutativity follows by swapping tensor factors in its two displayed values.

On the ordered basis $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$, each of $(m_L\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta_L)$, $\Delta_Lm_L$, and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L)(\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id})$ has outputs $1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $1\otimes1+X\otimes X$, $1\otimes1+X\otimes X$, and $1\otimes X+X\otimes1$. The Frobenius identities therefore hold. On a cube square, two changes on disjoint circles commute by tensor functoriality; two merges give the same composite by associativity of $m_L$; two splits give the same composite by coassociativity of $\Delta_L$; and a merge-split pair gives the same composite by the Frobenius identities just checked. In each case the cube signs on the two routes are opposite, so the square contribution to $d_L^2$ is zero. Every length-two path in the cube lies in one such square, so summing over squares proves $d_L^2=0$.

The terms of $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$ inherited from $\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2)$ have total quantum degree $0$ after the state shift. The new multiplication term $m_L(X\otimes X)=1$ changes the label degree from $-2$ to $1$, and the edge state shift adds $1$, so it raises $q$ by $4$. The new term $1\otimes1$ in $\Delta_L(X)$ changes label degree from $-1$ to $2$, and its edge state shift again adds $1$, so it raises $q$ by $4$. Thus every differential term preserves or raises $q$, making each $F^pC_L$ a subcomplex. The state set and each state module are finite, so only finitely many $q$-degrees occur and the filtration is finite. All algebra and cube checks use finite bases and no choice axiom.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram, order its crossings as $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and form the direct sum of state modules $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$ over all functions $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$. Here $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, each crossing is changed from its A-smoothing at $0$ to its B-smoothing at $1$, and the edge map is the multiplication $m$ for a merge or comultiplication $\Delta$ for a split, multiplied by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ on the edge at $c_j$. Then the sum $d$ of all edge maps satisfies $d^2=0$.

If the filtration on every $C_n$ is finite, the spectral sequence of the filtered chain complex stabilizes pointwise and naturally abuts to $H_n(C)$ with its image filtration. This homology filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform filtration bound in n is required.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. A **cochain complex in $\mathcal A$**
is a family of objects $(C^n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ together with morphisms
$$d^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$$
such that
$$d^{n+1}\circ d^n=0$$
for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

This page uses the reindexing convention that a cochain complex $C^\bullet$ may
also be read as the chain complex with $(C^\sharp)_n:=C^{-n}$ and
$d^\sharp_n:=d^{-n}$, so that lower and upper indices differ only by the sign
of the grading.

Let $A$ be an object of an abelian category. An **increasing filtration** is a specified family of subobjects $F_pA\subseteq A$, $p\in\mathbb Z$, with $F_pA\subseteq F_{p+1}A$. A **decreasing filtration** satisfies $F^{p+1}A\subseteq F^pA$. The translation on the same object is $F^pA=F_{-p}A$; translating back gives $F_pA=F^{-p}A$. A filtration-preserving morphism $f:A\to B$ factors on each piece as $F_pA\to F_pB\hookrightarrow B$ (or with upper indices). The restrictions are unique because the inclusions are monic. The ambient setting is [[def-abelian-category]].

derivations.claim: Put $a=1+X$ and $b=X-1$ in $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$. The relation $X^2=1$ gives $m_L(a\otimes a)=2a,\quad m_L(b\otimes b)=-2b,\quad m_L(a\otimes b)=m_L(b\otimes a)=0, \qquad \Delta_L(a)=a\otimes a,\quad\Delta_L(b)=b\otimes b.$ The counit takes value $1$ on each of $a,b$. In the basis $1,X$, the degree-preserving part of each saddle is the integral Khovanov saddle, and the only remaining terms replace $X\otimes X$ by $1$ under multiplication or replace $X$ by $1\otimes1$ under comultiplication. Each replacement raises the quantum degree by $4$, including the state shift, so the associated-graded differential is precisely the even Khovanov differential.

The projection of $D$ is a finite four-valent plane graph (with crossingless components as disjoint Jordan curves), so checkerboard-color its regions with the unbounded region white. Define the color of a region by the parity of intersections of a path from infinity to it with the projection; this is path-independent because every closed curve in the plane has even mod-$2$ intersection with the closed diagram. For each segment between crossing disks, assign label $a$ and direct it so that the black region is on its right, or assign label $b$ and direct it so that black is on its left. At a crossing, list the four incident segment ends clockwise as $1,2,3,4$, choosing the convention that sectors $(1,2)$ and $(3,4)$ are black, as in the local drawing. The arrows point outward/inward at ends $1,3$ according as their labels are $a/b$, and inward/outward at ends $2,4$ according as their labels are $a/b$. Thus the four patterns $aabb,abba,bbaa,baab$ are exactly those for which opposite ends have opposite arrows; in each case exactly one adjacent pairing connects equal labels and an incoming to an outgoing arrow. It is the oriented smoothing. All-equal patterns have two equal-label smoothings but do not orient the original crossing, while alternating and three-to-one patterns have no compatible smoothing. Thus, among segment labelings compatible with a smoothing at every crossing, having no all-equal crossing is equivalent to determining exactly one oriented state and an orientation of the link. For an oriented state, each circle has one label. Let $\delta(C)$ be the parity of the number of other Seifert circles separating it from infinity. The outside region of $C$ is black exactly when $\delta(C)=1$; its inside has the opposite color. As the interior is left of a counterclockwise circle and right of a clockwise circle, the black-right rule labels $C$ by $a$ exactly when $\delta(C)+\kappa(C)$ is even, where $\kappa(C)=1$ for counterclockwise and $0$ for clockwise. This is the parity rule in the Statement.

The cube has finitely many states and each state module is finite-dimensional, hence only finitely many quantum filtration levels occur. Reindex the cochain degrees and filtration by [F5], then apply [F4] to obtain a convergent spectral sequence with abutment $\operatorname{gr}H(C_L(D))$; reversing the filtration index changes only the page's filtration label. Index its first page as the associated-graded chain complex and its next as its cohomology. By step 1.1 and [F2], this cohomology is rational Khovanov cohomology. This is the convention in which the homology page is denoted $E_2$; changing page names does not change the limiting filtered homology.

Restrict an enhanced state to the diagram segments between crossing disks; its circle labels determine one segment labeling. From the operations in step 1.1, an edge map is nonzero exactly when the four labels at its crossing agree. Every nonzero edge preserves all segment labels, so the complex is a direct sum over segment labelings. For a fixed labeling, each all-equal crossing is a free coordinate with both smoothings and an invertible saddle; each other crossing has at most one compatible smoothing. If any crossing has no compatible smoothing the summand is zero; otherwise its compatible states form a Boolean cube on precisely the all-equal crossings.

On any nonempty cube from step 2.2, every edge coefficient is nonzero in $\mathbb Q$. Let $u(e)$ be the coefficient of a directed edge and let $s(e)=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v_i}$ be the standard cube sign on the edge changing coordinate $j$. The equation $d^2=0$ gives $u(e_1)u(e_2)=-u(e_3)u(e_4)$ around each square, and the standard signs satisfy the same equation. Hence $u(e)/s(e)$ has product $1$ around every square. Rescale each vertex basis by the product of these ratios along a path from a fixed vertex; square faces generate all path changes in a Boolean cube, so the rescaling is path-independent and identifies its differential with the standard tensor differential. If there is a free coordinate, its factor is $\mathbb Q\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathbb Q$; contracting that factor with the tensor-product Koszul sign contracts the whole cube. If there is no free coordinate, the cube is a single zero-differential line. When $D$ is empty, this is the unique empty-state line $\mathbb Q$, whose class is the empty-tensor unit. In all cases, step 1.2 identifies the singleton lines bijectively with the orientations of the link, so they form a basis of Lee homology.

In the canonical basis $a=1+X$, $b=X-1$, one has $Xa=a$, $Xb=-b$. The checkerboard convention for the canonical labels is unchanged outside the disk. At one fixed mark on each component its sign determines the orientation of that component; consequently the $2^c$ orientation classes are distinct simultaneous eigenlines of the exterior marked actions. A Reidemeister homology isomorphism intertwining those actions must carry each eigenline to the line with the same signs, and cannot kill it. Thus it carries each orientation class to a nonzero multiple of the class with the induced orientation. In the basis $a,b$ the Morse maps are $\eta_L(1)=\tfrac12(a-b)$, $m_L(aa)=2a$, $m_L(bb)=-2b$, $m_L(ab)=m_L(ba)=0$, $\Delta_L(a)=aa$, $\Delta_L(b)=bb$, and $\epsilon_L(a)=\epsilon_L(b)=1$. An orientation extends across an oriented band exactly in the opposite-arrow case. The exterior checkerboard colors remain fixed, so the surviving equal label is the canonical label after the saddle. A birth creates precisely the two possibilities with nonzero coefficients. A split or a band within one surface component extends its orientation uniquely and multiplies its coefficient by a nonzero scalar. A band joining distinct components retains precisely the compatible choices and kills the others: each orientation of the joined component restricts to a unique compatible pair, so no two retained terms cancel. For a death the disappearing boundary circle belongs to a surface component with another boundary, unless that component becomes closed. A closed component of a partial surface cannot later join another component, and would be a closed component of $S$; connectedness and its incoming boundary exclude this. Hence exactly one permitted orientation extends either incoming orientation, and its coefficient is nonzero. The two input classes map to nonzero multiples of the two output classes.

Assign to a planar isotopy the relabeling of state circles, to a Reidemeister move the filtered map of [F3], and to a Morse event the cube map induced by the corresponding Lee Frobenius operation in [F2]. These are actual cochain maps: the move disk misses the crossings, and its unsigned operation commutes with every cube saddle by associativity, coassociativity and the Frobenius/unit/counit identities proved for [F2]; the crossing set and its cube signs remain fixed. citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Its rational Lee homology is a two-dimensional vector space. For every finite regular diagram of $K$, the two homology classes obtained from the two orientations by the oriented-resolution parity-of-nesting rule form a basis, and the induced quantum filtration is independent of the diagram.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

derivations.claim: In the positively oriented source chart of [A2], take the over-tangent to be $(1,1)$. Positivity forces the under-tangent to be $(-1,1)$ rather than $(1,-1)$, since their determinants with the over-tangent are $2$ and $-2$. The incoming endpoints are therefore southwest and southeast, and the outgoing endpoints northeast and northwest. The orientation-preserving smoothing pairs southwest with northwest and southeast with northeast: exactly the A-smoothing. Reversing both strand arrows gives the other positive orientation case and retains those same pairs. Thus every positive oriented smoothing is the $0$-resolution.

By step 1.1, every oriented smoothing is the $0$-resolution, so the canonical cycle lies in cohomological degree $0$. There is no chain group in degree $-1$, hence this cycle is not altered by adding a boundary. Expanding each of its $k$ circle labels $a=1+X$ or $b=X-1$ in the homogeneous basis, the unique term of least quantum degree is obtained by choosing $X$ on every circle; its coefficient is $1$ or $-1$. Its quantum degree is the state shift $n$ plus $k$ labels of degree $-1$, namely $n-k$. Therefore its induced filtration level is $s_{\min}(K)=n-k$.

The formula [F2] for $s$ is diagram-independent under the AC$_\omega$ branch [A1]. Substitution of the value from step 2.1 gives $s(K)=n-k+1$. If $n=0$, the positive diagram is the crossingless unknot, whose oriented resolution has $k=1$, so the same calculation gives $s=0$. The state expansion itself is finite and choice-free.

derivations.claim: On $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$ use $\langle u,v\rangle=\epsilon_L(uv)$, whose matrix in the basis $1,X$ is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Number the crossings identically on $D$ and its mirror. For a mirror vertex $w$, its corresponding original vertex is $v=1-w$. The local smoothing chart interchanges A and B under reflection, so their resolved circles agree. On the dual complex put $(C^\vee)^i=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(C^{-i},\mathbb Q)$ and $d^\vee=(d)^*$; this convention squares to zero directly. For the mirror edge changing coordinate $j$, the original reversed edge has sign $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$, while its mirror sign is $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}w_k}=(-1)^{j-1}(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$. Multiply the tensor-pairing identification on mirror vertex $w$ by $\sigma(w)=(-1)^{\sum_j(j-1)w_j}$. Since $\sigma(w+e_j)/\sigma(w)=(-1)^{j-1}$, this makes every edge commute with the transposed original edge. It is therefore an actual cochain isomorphism, including cube signs. With $n=n_++n_-$, complementation gives $i'=-i$ and state shift $|w|+n'_{+}-2n'_{-}=-|v|-n_++2n_-$, the negative original shift. Dual tensor labels have opposite label degrees as well, giving $q'=-q$. Reversing the knot orientation leaves crossing signs and resolutions unchanged, so the same isomorphism applies to $K^\dagger$.

For a finite filtered cochain complex $C$, the just-described dual quantum filtration is $F^pC^\vee=\operatorname{Ann}(F^{1-p}C)$ in complementary cohomological degrees. Evaluation induces a perfect pairing $H(C^\vee)\times H(C)\to\mathbb Q$: cocycles are exactly the functionals vanishing on boundaries, and coboundaries are exactly those vanishing on cycles, by finite elimination. Its induced homology filtration is exactly the annihilator filtration. Indeed one direction follows by evaluating representatives. Conversely a homology functional vanishing on classes represented by cycles in $F^{1-p}C$ defines a functional on the sum of the cycle space and $F^{1-p}C$, using its given values on cycles and zero on the latter subspace. The intersection condition makes this well-defined. Extend it across a finite vector-space complement; it is a cocycle because it vanishes on boundaries and represents the required dual class in $F^p$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a connected compact oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with product collars and oriented boundary $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$ for oriented knots $K_0,K_1$ in the standard three-sphere. A **finite movie** for $S$ is a finite ordered sequence of regular-level link diagrams whose changes are planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves, births, saddles or deaths. Such a movie defines a map on rational Lee homology that preserves the induced decreasing filtration with degree $\chi(S)=-2g$. The map is an isomorphism; consequently
$$
|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le 2g.
$$

Assume countable choice. Let $F\subset B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi:B^4\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, such that $\Psi(F)\cap B^4_\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\Psi(F)\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon\cong S^3\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.

derivations.claim: For the standard crossingless unknot diagram, the Lee complex is the one-term vector space $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$ with basis $1,X$ in quantum degrees $1,-1$ and zero differential. Its induced filtration levels are therefore $s_{\max}(U)=1$ and $s_{\min}(U)=-1$, so [F2] gives $s(U)=0$.

Let $F\subset B^4$ be any connected smooth orientable proper spanning surface of genus $g$ with boundary $K$. Apply [F4] under the countable-choice hypothesis [A1]. It moves and flattens a small interior surface disk by ambient diffeomorphisms fixed on a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar, then removes an actual concentric round ball. The remaining round shell is explicitly $S^3\times I$, with unchanged boundary knot $K$, an inner standard unknot and product collars. Its surface is connected of the same genus $g$ and has Euler characteristic $-2g$; reverse its direction if needed. This uses neither a slice-only Statement for a positive-genus surface nor a claim about arbitrary embedded four-ball complements.

Apply the Lee cobordism construction to this surface and to its reverse. By [F3], each map is a filtered isomorphism of degree $-2g$. Choose a nonzero class of maximal level in $V_K$; its image is nonzero in $V_U$ and has level at least $s_{\max}(K)-2g$, which is at most $s_{\max}(U)=1$. Hence $s_{\max}(K)\le1+2g$ and $s(K)\le2g$. Apply the reverse map to a nonzero class of maximal level in $V_U$: its nonzero image in $V_K$ has level at least $1-2g$, so $s_{\max}(K)\ge1-2g$ and $s(K)\ge-2g$.

Under [A1], [F1] supplies a nonempty set of smooth spanning-surface genera with a least element. Minimize $g$ over $F$ in step 1.2. Step 2.1 then gives the asserted inequality. This gives the inequality in the Statement.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with at least one component, ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and a marked point $p$ on the projected link away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. If a point away from the saddle disks is marked on a component of the diagram, the vertexwise comparison commutes with its marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

For a finite planar odd resolution cube with the prescribed full face signs, a Reidemeister I or II move supported away from the marked point induces a normalized bigraded chain homotopy equivalence over the right ring $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalence, inverse and contraction are finite integer matrices in exterior quotients, exterior products, and projections to the two coefficients of a small-circle generator. Their reductions modulo two are the corresponding even Khovanov cancellation maps. The result holds for every exterior closure of the move disk and every orientation of its strands, and is choice-free.

For finite based diagrams differing by Reidemeister III in a disk missing the mark, their normalized odd complexes, with the prescribed full face signs, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent over the right ring $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalences and homotopies are integral and reduce modulo two to the even local cancellation equivalence. They apply to every exterior closure, including closures in which several local arcs belong to the same resolution circle. Together with the marked Reidemeister I and II contractions this proves invariance under every finite based Reidemeister sequence. No choice axiom is needed for these finite constructions.

Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

Let two finite based knot diagrams be joined along their marked arcs in a planar pointed connected-sum diagram, without new crossings. Use odd edge assignments realizing the full prescribed face products, including the zero-composite faces. The odd complexes admit a normalized bigraded right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism
$$ C_o(D_1)\otimes_{\mathbb A}C_o(D_2)\{-1\}\ \cong\ C_o(D_1\#D_2), $$
and the Bar–Natan complexes admit the corresponding marked $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$-linear chain isomorphism. In the odd case the induced signs realize the full prescribed face products, so admissible sign comparison applies, including zero-composite faces. The two isomorphisms agree after reduction modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ under the statewise comparison. Their construction is finite and choice-free.

Let a finite oriented based regular link diagram, with its ordered crossing disks and crossing arrows, lie on an oriented two-sphere. Choose any two orientation-preserving planar coordinate presentations whose omitted points miss the diagram and all crossing disks. Transport the diagram, crossing arrows, over/under information and mark by these coordinates; keep the same crossing order. Circle relabelling gives grading-preserving marked-module chain isomorphisms between their integral odd complexes with transported full admissible edge signs, and between their integral Bar–Natan complexes. In particular the full odd face prescription, including zero-composite faces, is unchanged by the choice of omitted point.

For independently chosen edge assignments satisfying that full prescription, compose the odd relabelling with vertexwise signs. The resulting odd and Bar–Natan isomorphisms have inverse maps, are respectively right linear over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, and give a strictly commuting square under the statewise reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$. Their inverses give the inverse square. Whenever the endpoint triples satisfy the LEO hypotheses, these maps therefore give local maps in both directions; this applies in particular to knot triples once their separate foundations have been established. The Bar–Natan maps are already chain isomorphisms before localization. The construction is finite and requires no choice axiom. This assertion concerns recharting the same spherical diagram, not transporting a mark through a crossing of a fixed planar diagram.

Assume countable choice. Every prescribed finite regular oriented knot diagram with a specified marked point away from its crossings admits a compatible long endpoint presentation by finitely many planar isotopies and one orientation-preserving spherical rotation recharting. All crossing labels, crossing arrows if specified, strand orientations, over/under data and the mark are transported. No crossing is created, removed, or passed through the mark. The final planar diagram has a round disk containing every crossing and all of the diagram except a single crossing-free exterior closing arc carrying the mark; the disk boundary meets the diagram transversely in exactly two points. A neighborhood of that arc can be used as the protected marked neighborhood in a long-tangle movie.

The recharting omits a point in a face adjacent to the marked germ. Its spherical rotation extends by an explicit orientation-preserving linear map of $S^3$, and the planar normalizations have actual spatial coordinate lifts. Thus the construction records an orientation-preserving spatial identification of the represented marked endpoint knot, rather than declaring its coordinate identifications to be identities. A representative can be chosen with the exterior arc at constant projection height and with product collars at its two cut points. This is a geometric existence assertion. It asserts neither a purely planar protected Reidemeister comparison nor an algebraic invariance theorem. The construction uses only finite selections and explicit maps, so in fact introduces no choice beyond the stated branch.

Assume countable choice. Let $F:S^1\times[0,1]\to S^3$ be a smooth isotopy of oriented knots, stationary in end collars, with a specified marked source point. Suppose its two endpoint diagrams are regular compatible long presentations with the same standard oriented exterior marked arc, parametrized identically on a neighborhood of that point. Use the corresponding spatial endpoint coordinates, in which this common marked arc is a standard small round arc through the stereographic point at infinity; its puncture is closed in the planar diagrams by the same standard exterior arc. Then these prescribed endpoint diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves, whose closed support disks miss the mark. The marked neighborhood remains fixed. There are no births, saddles or deaths. The movie represents the given marked isotopy up to a spatial coordinate family equal to the identity in both end collars and a small isotopy relative those collars.

Here compatible long endpoints include the displayed common oriented arc and its spatial coordinate identifications. This statement does not silently identify arbitrary physical endpoint coordinates. Spherical endpoint recharting may first be used to choose such common compatible presentations; no algebraic invariance of that recharting or of these movies is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

derivations.claim: By [F2], choose the full admissible face assignment. The coefficient of every height-two state in the square of the differential is zero, since the two signed saddle composites cancel, including the faces where both composites vanish. The normalized saddle grading is that of [F1]. Each state is a finite free right $\mathbb A$-module: use the basis of exterior products of the augmentation-zero differences $Z_j-Z_p$, followed by the optional marked factor $Z_p$. Thus the actual odd complex exists, with the asserted bigrading and marked action. The construction in [F2] is finite and uses no additional choice.

Modulo two, send each exterior circle generator to the even $X$-label on that circle. The merge quotient becomes the even product, and multiplication by $C_1-C_2$ becomes the even split map, since all signs disappear. The Bar–Natan formulas of [F1] reduce modulo $(2,h)$ to the same product and split. These identifications also carry appending $Z_p$ to multiplication by the marked $X$. Therefore the comparison is a bigraded marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism, and in particular a chain homotopy equivalence.

The localized proof in [F4] decomposes the enhanced-state cube into Boolean summands in the basis $A=X,B=h-X$, contracts each non-singleton summand by unit identity pivots, and does so over the marked ring because the marked label is constant on a summand. The two singleton knot states are its orientations, in degree zero and odd quantum parity. The two idempotents $X/h$ and $1-X/h$ identify their span with one regular rank-one localized coefficient module. This supplies the required chain homotopy equivalence, including the module-linearity of its homotopies.

For a planar pointed sum, [F5] gives the right-linear odd map using the reduced decomposition $\Lambda V=\Lambda\ker(\operatorname{aug})\otimes\mathbb A$. On reduced exterior degrees $r_1,r_2$ its formula is $(-1)^{r_1\sigma_2}(u_1\wedge u_2)\otimes a_1a_2$. Its sign is independent of both marked factors, so it is balanced and right-linear; its internal and mixed full face products are verified in [F5]. The BN map is marked multiplication with vertex sign $(-1)^{n_-^{(1)}|v_2|}$, accounting for normalized cochain tensor signs. Both merge two circles into one and have the displayed quantum shift $\{-1\}$. Their reductions agree with the same even marked multiplication. The admissible sign comparison in [F2] transfers this to any admissible representatives. This proves the connected-sum clauses.

**Arbitrary prescribed based endpoints.** For a finite pair of based diagrams first use [F7] with the same local coordinates at their marks: each oriented marked tangent is the positive real axis. After straightening their crossing-free germs, choose one common radius $r$, one $0<\epsilon<\min(r/4,1/4)$ and one $R$ between $B=(1+\epsilon r)/(r-\epsilon)$ and $1/\epsilon$. The same rotation rechart $w=-(1+\overline a z)/(z-a)$, $a=i\epsilon$, then acts on both. Their exterior arcs are literally the same $w(x)$, with the same cut parameters $x=\pm c$, where $c^2=(1-R^2\epsilon^2)/(R^2-\epsilon^2)$. Flatten their height to zero as in [F7]. They have the same oriented geodesic marked germ and the same compatible spatial endpoint model. If puncturing spatially at the mark changes the planar chart, use [F8]'s explicit endpoint comparison: move the pole within the exterior cap, restrict the chart transitions to the common compact tangle disk, extend this compact-disk embedding isotopy to the plane, and use the image of the common closing arc. These are actual planar isotopies to the punctured-and-reclosed diagrams, not a claimed equality of drawings under pole change. All endpoint coordinate identifications are recorded in [F7] and [F8].

**Full based diagram invariance.** Suppose the prescribed based diagrams represent isotopic oriented knots. Reparametrize a representing smooth knot isotopy so that its marked source point reaches the specified endpoint marks; an orientation-preserving circle reparametrization can be chosen through rotations in its source parameter and made stationary in end collars. Compose with the explicit endpoint coordinate isotopies from step 1.5. The resulting endpoints have the common long model. By [F8] this isotopy has a finite protected movie containing only R1, R2, R3 and planar isotopies; its relative contraction ensures identity spatial coordinate maps at both ends. No birth, saddle or death is used to infer an odd equivalence. Each R move has the integral marked chain homotopy inverses and homotopies of [F3], and their common even reductions are those of [F4]. The spherical endpoint normalizations have the explicit integral marked isomorphisms and inverse squares of [F6]. Compose these actual maps and their inverses with the planar endpoint isotopies. Thus the original arbitrary prescribed based diagrams have graded marked odd chain homotopy equivalences, with the asserted comparison; the corresponding BN maps are also graded marked chain homotopy equivalences. This handles arbitrary basepoint positions through the geometric endpoint normalization and does not assume a false protected planar comparison between an arbitrary diagram and its exterior rechart.

**Finite ordering and sign choices.** A different full admissible assignment changes the odd complex by the vertex-sign marked isomorphism of [F2]; no invariance assertion about all weak square-compatible candidates is needed. Circle reorderings are actual exterior basis changes. Crossing reorderings transport cube coordinates and the full odd edge assignment. On the BN side a transposition of adjacent crossings $i,j$ changes the ordinary cube-sign convention by the vertex factor $(-1)^{v_i v_j}$: on an $i$-edge its ratio is $(-1)^{v_j}$, on a $j$-edge it is $(-1)^{v_i}$, and on all other edges it is one, exactly the change in the number of preceding 1-coordinates. Products of such transpositions handle every finite crossing permutation. The same factors can be used on the transported odd assignment; they preserve its full face products and reduce to one modulo two. Hence ordering changes and the choices in the coherent full admissible family preserve the claimed marked chain-homotopy type and common reduction.

**Concordance consumers with arbitrary endpoints.** For a collared oriented annulus between any prescribed based knot diagrams choose a proper marked arc between its boundary marks, constant on the given end collars; a product parametrization of the annulus gives such an arc by a smooth angular path between the two marks. Normalize the finite endpoint pair by step 1.5 and carry the annulus through those recorded orientation-preserving spatial endpoint identifications, using their isotopies on end collars. It now has compatible common long endpoints. Apply [F9]'s actual relative four-dimensional arc straightening, followed by its protected strip/puncture, finite Morse and relative projection construction. Its coordinates can retain the common endpoint strips: the center–tangent contraction and parameter-dependent velocity extension in [F8] apply to the family of strip intervals along the already monotone marked arc, not just to whole level knots, and give spatial coordinates identity in both end collars. Thus the required supplied protected movie exists for these endpoints. Its odd and BN maps are those of [F4], with degree the annulus Euler characteristic zero and the exact marked mod-two square; [F4] proves that the localized BN composite is a marked-ring homotopy equivalence. Compose with [F6] and the planar endpoint isomorphisms to return to the original prescribed diagrams. Read the annulus backwards for a local map in the other direction. This uses no odd movie-independence assertion and does not require any individual birth or death map to be a localized equivalence. Together with the tensor calculation in step 1.4 and the R-only invariance in step 2.1, it proves every assertion of the Statement in its full arbitrary-based-diagram scope. Countable choice is exactly the retained geometric extension/genericity hypothesis; all new algebraic maps and finite endpoint choices require no additional choice.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with at least one component, ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and a marked point $p$ on the projected link away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite regular based oriented knot diagram, the odd exterior-algebra cube admits a square-compatible edge assignment and defines a bigraded cochain complex; its mod-2 reduction is chain homotopy equivalent as a marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-complex to the Bar–Natan complex reduced modulo $(2,h)$. After inverting $h$, the Bar–Natan complex is chain homotopy equivalent to one free rank-one module in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree over the localized coefficient algebra. Based diagram changes preserve the odd complex up to chain homotopy equivalence, and pointed connected sums give the chain-level tensor product over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ for the odd complex and over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$ for the Bar–Natan complex, in each case with the quantum shift $\{-1\}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let a finite oriented based regular link diagram, with its ordered crossing disks and crossing arrows, lie on an oriented two-sphere. Choose any two orientation-preserving planar coordinate presentations whose omitted points miss the diagram and all crossing disks. Transport the diagram, crossing arrows, over/under information and mark by these coordinates; keep the same crossing order. Circle relabelling gives grading-preserving marked-module chain isomorphisms between their integral odd complexes with transported full admissible edge signs, and between their integral Bar–Natan complexes. In particular the full odd face prescription, including zero-composite faces, is unchanged by the choice of omitted point.

For independently chosen edge assignments satisfying that full prescription, compose the odd relabelling with vertexwise signs. The resulting odd and Bar–Natan isomorphisms have inverse maps, are respectively right linear over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, and give a strictly commuting square under the statewise reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$. Their inverses give the inverse square. Whenever the endpoint triples satisfy the LEO hypotheses, these maps therefore give local maps in both directions; this applies in particular to knot triples once their separate foundations have been established. The Bar–Natan maps are already chain isomorphisms before localization. The construction is finite and requires no choice axiom. This assertion concerns recharting the same spherical diagram, not transporting a mark through a crossing of a fixed planar diagram.

Assume countable choice. Every prescribed finite regular oriented knot diagram with a specified marked point away from its crossings admits a compatible long endpoint presentation by finitely many planar isotopies and one orientation-preserving spherical rotation recharting. All crossing labels, crossing arrows if specified, strand orientations, over/under data and the mark are transported. No crossing is created, removed, or passed through the mark. The final planar diagram has a round disk containing every crossing and all of the diagram except a single crossing-free exterior closing arc carrying the mark; the disk boundary meets the diagram transversely in exactly two points. A neighborhood of that arc can be used as the protected marked neighborhood in a long-tangle movie.

The recharting omits a point in a face adjacent to the marked germ. Its spherical rotation extends by an explicit orientation-preserving linear map of $S^3$, and the planar normalizations have actual spatial coordinate lifts. Thus the construction records an orientation-preserving spatial identification of the represented marked endpoint knot, rather than declaring its coordinate identifications to be identities. A representative can be chosen with the exterior arc at constant projection height and with product collars at its two cut points. This is a geometric existence assertion. It asserts neither a purely planar protected Reidemeister comparison nor an algebraic invariance theorem. The construction uses only finite selections and explicit maps, so in fact introduces no choice beyond the stated branch.

Assume countable choice. Let $F:S^1\times[0,1]\to S^3$ be a smooth isotopy of oriented knots, stationary in end collars, with a specified marked source point. Suppose its two endpoint diagrams are regular compatible long presentations with the same standard oriented exterior marked arc, parametrized identically on a neighborhood of that point. Use the corresponding spatial endpoint coordinates, in which this common marked arc is a standard small round arc through the stereographic point at infinity; its puncture is closed in the planar diagrams by the same standard exterior arc. Then these prescribed endpoint diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves, whose closed support disks miss the mark. The marked neighborhood remains fixed. There are no births, saddles or deaths. The movie represents the given marked isotopy up to a spatial coordinate family equal to the identity in both end collars and a small isotopy relative those collars.

Here compatible long endpoints include the displayed common oriented arc and its spatial coordinate identifications. This statement does not silently identify arbitrary physical endpoint coordinates. Spherical endpoint recharting may first be used to choose such common compatible presentations; no algebraic invariance of that recharting or of these movies is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

Let two finite based knot diagrams be joined along their marked arcs in a planar pointed connected-sum diagram, without new crossings. Use odd edge assignments realizing the full prescribed face products, including the zero-composite faces. The odd complexes admit a normalized bigraded right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism
$$ C_o(D_1)\otimes_{\mathbb A}C_o(D_2)\{-1\}\ \cong\ C_o(D_1\#D_2), $$
and the Bar–Natan complexes admit the corresponding marked $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$-linear chain isomorphism. In the odd case the induced signs realize the full prescribed face products, so admissible sign comparison applies, including zero-composite faces. The two isomorphisms agree after reduction modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ under the statewise comparison. Their construction is finite and choice-free.

derivations.claim: Local equivalence is reflexive because each triple has its identity local map, symmetric by its definition as maps in both directions, and transitive because the composites of local maps remain module chain maps, their localized Bar–Natan maps are composites of homotopy equivalences, and the two mod-$(2,h)$ squares compose up to the sum of their module-linear homotopies. Thus local equivalence is an equivalence relation.

The tensor product of two LEO triples is again a LEO triple: tensoring finite free complexes preserves finite freeness, tensoring the reductions gives the homotopy equivalence $f\otimes f'$, and tensoring the localized rank-one equivalences gives a rank-one equivalence over the localized coefficient algebra. Tensor products of local maps are local maps because tensor products preserve chain homotopies and homotopy equivalences between these free localized complexes. Hence the shifted tensor product is associative and respects local-equivalence classes. The graded symmetry $u\otimes v\mapsto(-1)^{|u||v|}v\otimes u$ gives commutativity, and the unknot triple is the unit because its complexes are $\mathbb A\{1\}$ and $\mathbb R\{1\}$.

For $T=(C,D,f)$ define $T^*=(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,\mathbb A)\{2\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,\mathbb R)\{2\},f^*)$, where $f^*$ is the transpose induced by a homotopy inverse $g$ to the reduced equivalence $f$. Finite freeness lets dualization commute with reduction and localization; it preserves chain homotopies and chain homotopy equivalences. Thus $T^*$ satisfies the LEO conditions, and dualizing both maps and the module-linear homotopy in a local-map square gives a local map in the reverse direction. The finite-free tensor-Hom isomorphisms identify $T\otimes T^*$ with $(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,C)\{1\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,D)\{1\},F)$, where on reductions $F(\eta)=f\eta g$. The coevaluation maps from the unknot triple send $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_C$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$. The reduced square commutes up to the module-linear homotopy $H$ from $fg\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$, since $F(\mathrm{id}_C)=fg$. After inverting $h$, the BN coevaluation map $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(D[h^{-1}],D[h^{-1}])$ sends $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_D$; under a chosen homotopy equivalence $D[h^{-1}]\simeq\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ it is homotopic to the identity map of the rank-one endomorphism complex, so it is a homotopy equivalence by [F2]. The reverse evaluation maps are the graded evaluations $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ on the finite-free tensor-Hom identifications, with the standard Hom differential $d\phi=-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi d$. They are chain maps because the two terms in $d(\phi\otimes c)$ evaluate to $-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$ and $+(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$. For the reduced evaluation square choose a separate module-linear homotopy $\ell$ on $\bar C=C\otimes\mathbb F_2$ satisfying $gf-\mathrm{id}_{\bar C}=d\ell+\ell d$; the homotopy $H$ above acts on $\bar D$ and is not used here. Under the graded flip to the dual-first tensor order, the two reduced evaluation composites are $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ and $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(gf(c))$, so the reduced square commutes up to $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(\ell(c))$ (over $\mathbb F_2$ the Koszul signs are one), and after localization evaluation identifies with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(\mathbb R[h^{-1}],\mathbb R[h^{-1}])\to\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$, an isomorphism. Hence the two evaluation maps are local maps in both directions, proving $T\otimes T^*$ locally equivalent to the unknot triple and $T^*$ is an inverse.
