citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

derivations.claim: **Small marked arcs and their relative center–tangent data.** Parametrize a uniformly small marked interval by oriented arclength $v$ near zero, smoothly in the isotopy parameter $t$; the resulting reparametrization changes neither knot nor mark and is stationary in the end collars. Let $b(t)=F(0,t)$ and let $u(t)$ be its unit tangent. Identify $S^3$ with unit quaternions. The imaginary unit quaternion $c(t)=b(t)^{-1}u(t)$ lies in $S^2$, and $(b(t),c(t))$ is a smooth loop in $S^3\times S^2$, constant in the end collars. The two endpoint marked arcs are the same by hypothesis. In exponential coordinates at $b(t)$ the small actual arc has the form $vu(t)+O(v^2)$, with derivative $u(t)+O(v)$ uniformly in $t$. Interpolating its error to zero gives a smooth family of embedded intervals for a sufficiently small uniform width: projection onto $u(t)$ has strictly positive derivative. This interpolation is stationary in the end collars if their common model is taken to be the geodesic round arc, as stipulated. Its inverse will later restore the actual marked germ.

**An explicit contraction fixes both parameter ends.** A smooth loop in either $S^d$, $d=2,3$, misses a point. Indeed a derivative bound makes its $n$ equal parameter intervals map into $n$ balls of radius $C/n$; their total spherical $d$-volume is at most $C'n^{1-d}$, which tends to zero. They cannot cover the positive-volume sphere. Choose one omitted point for each of the two loops from step 1.1. Stereographic coordinates from those points send each loop into Euclidean space. The straight interpolation from its constant endpoint value to its value at $t$ contracts it through loops constant on the same end collars; inverse stereographic projection gives smooth loops $b_s(t),c_s(t)$, with $s=0$ constant and $s=1$ the given data. Thus $$A_{s,t}(v)=b_s(t)\bigl(\cos v+c_s(t)\sin v\bigr)$$ is a smooth family of geodesic marked interval embeddings, with $A_{0,t}$ the common standard arc and $A_{s,t}$ equal to it in both end collars. Concatenate with the inverse error interpolation in step 1.1, using stationary smooth parameter joins. This constructs a two-parameter family of embedded intervals from the constant common arc to the actual moving marked arcs; at $t$ in either end collar the entire family is the constant arc.

**Relative ambient coordinates really are identity at both ends.** Extend the velocity in the contraction parameter $s$ of step 2.1 by the actual construction in [F1], with $t$ an additional parameter. To spell out the relative point: the track in $S^3\times[0,1]_s\times[0,1]_t$ is embedded because its last two coordinates retain $s,t$ and each interval slice is embedded. In finite track charts extend the three spatial velocity components constantly in normal coordinates, patch by a smooth partition, and apply a compact cutoff equal to one on the smaller interval track. The prescribed velocity is zero on both $t$ end collars; choose all extended components zero there, using charts of the constant product arc on those collars and a cutoff in $t$ on their complement. Integrate in $s$. Uniqueness of the ODE gives a smooth family $H_t$ of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms with $H_t(A_{0,t})$ the actual marked interval and $H_t=\mathrm{id}$ on both time end collars. Consequently $H_t^{-1}F_t$ is a knot isotopy retaining exactly the given endpoints and fixing one common marked interval for every $t$. This contraction argument is necessary: simply extending the moving interval in the parameter $t$ would not by itself force the terminal ambient map to be the identity.

**Puncture without changing height or endpoints.** Apply the product-strip and puncture construction of [F2] to this fixed common interval, with spatial coordinates independent of $t$. In a smaller neighborhood the knots agree with that interval for all $t$; compactness gives uniform separation from the rest after shortening it once. Puncturing at its central point gives an isotopy of compact long tangles, fixed on their two spatial end collars, closed by one fixed exterior arc carrying the mark. The spatial coordinate changes in step 3.1 were level-preserving, so its trace is still exactly a cylinder of knot embeddings with time coordinate $t$. In particular the restriction of time to this cylinder has nonzero derivative everywhere. There is no need for a Morse perturbation, and none is made. There is an explicit planar endpoint comparison if the displayed closed diagrams initially use a pole in the adjacent face rather than the spatial puncture at the mark. Write their common round compact projection disk as $D=\{|z|\le R\}$ and their common marked point as $p$, where $|p|>R$. Choose a small marked germ and $\delta>0$ so that its closed neighborhood misses $W=\{|z|<R+\delta\}$. Set $$b_u=\frac{uR^2}{\overline p},\qquad f_u(z)=\frac{z-b_u}{1-\overline b_u z/R^2},\qquad 0\le u\le1.$$ These are disk automorphisms, starting at the identity: on $|z|=R$ one has $|z-b_u|^2=R^2|1-\overline b_u z/R^2|^2$, and their inverse fractional linear maps have the same disk property. Their complex derivative has nonzero numerator $1-|b_u|^2/R^2>0$. Their pole is $p/u$, with infinity at $u=0$, so it stays outside $D$ and ends at the marked point. Thus $f_u|_D$ is an actual smooth isotopy of compact disk embeddings onto $D$, including $u=1$. It is an orientation-preserving coordinate chart on the punctured projection sphere. Its endpoint pole is the spatial puncture point; postcomposition by a positive planar similarity identifies it with a rotation-induced stereographic chart with that pole if such a chart is used for the spatial coordinates. One may instead retain this very chart in the puncture construction. Apply [F1] to $f_u|_D$ in the plane, with extension support in $W$. Its disk velocity is tangent to the boundary; the extension theorem for a compact source with boundary applies and gives an ambient plane isotopy $\Phi_u$ equal to $f_u$ on $D$ and identity outside $W$. Consequently it fixes the specified marked germ pointwise throughout. Choose the long closing arc to be $\Phi_1$ of the original common exterior arc. It is outside $D$, since $\Phi_1$ preserves $D$, and retains exactly the same marked germ. This supplies protected planar isotopies from the displayed endpoints to the punctured-and-reclosed endpoints; prepend and append those isotopies. For two normalized endpoints use the same $D,p,b_u,\Phi_u$ and closing arc. No arbitrary ambient extension or equality of different planar charts is being assumed: both the prescribed endpoint diagrams and their fixed marked germ are retained by the recorded relative extension.

**Relative finite projection genericity.** Repeat the family of [F3] on this compact tangle isotopy with bumps zero on smaller parameter end collars and spatial tangle-end collars. At every movable source point these bumps are positive, so the same finite monomial Hermite interpolation prescribes the required independent jets; its evaluations at protected source points are not needed. The exterior closing arc and the two joining collars have fixed regular projection, separated from the compact moving portion. Thus no bad projection stratum involving the protected mark is present. On the moving portion the cusp, tangent-double and triple equations, exclusions of their coincidences and higher degeneracies, and deleted-diagonal estimates are precisely those proved in [F3]. Arbitrarily small parameter choices give finitely many separated generic events relative the stationary endpoint diagrams. The perturbations change spatial coordinates of the slice embeddings only, so their trace remains a height-submersive cylinder. Straight interpolation between the original and sufficiently close perturbed slice maps is an embedding isotopy by the uniform local immersion and distant-pair separation bounds used in [F3]. It is fixed on every protected collar.

The event identification in [F3] gives only oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves; between them the projected decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy. Each exceptional event has compact support inside the projection disk and therefore misses the fixed marked exterior arc. The finite time list yields the required sequence. No surface critical point has been introduced, so births, saddles and deaths do not occur. Undoing $H_t^{-1}$ identifies its trace with the given marked isotopy, up to the small relative perturbation in step 5.1. Since $H_t$ is identity on both end collars, the spatial endpoint identifications are retained exactly; the explicitly recorded planar endpoint isotopies in step 4.1 return the displayed prescribed diagrams. This proves the stated relative comparison and no algebraic map assertion.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface, with product collars and boundary the finite oriented links $-L_0$ and $L_1$ in the two ends. Components of $S$ and either boundary link may be empty. After an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller prescribed end collars, $S$ has a finite movie consisting of planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2 and R3, births, oriented saddle band moves, and deaths. All exceptional times are distinct. The movie's actual smoothly embedded trace is ambient isotopic to the given $S$ relative to those collars, with its boundary orientations and parametrizations retained. Prescribed regular endpoint diagrams may be retained. This is movie existence; it asserts no equivalence theorem for two movies.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

If $M$ is a compact smooth manifold and $f:M\to\mathbb R$ is a Morse function,
then $f$ has only finitely many critical points.

Let $W$ be a compact smooth manifold with boundary and let $f:W\to\mathbb R$ be
a Morse function with finitely many critical points, all interior and none in a
closed neighbourhood $C$ of $\partial W$. Then every $C^\infty$ neighbourhood of
$f$ contains a Morse function $g$ with $g=f$ on $C$, the same critical points and
the same Hessian at each of them, and distinct critical values.

$f$, and let $\lambda$ be the index of $p$. If $n=\dim M$, then there are local
coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ centered at $p$ in which

$$f=f(p)-\sum_{i=1}^{\lambda}(x^i)^2+\sum_{i=\lambda+1}^{n}(x^i)^2.$$

For $n=0$, both sums are empty.

isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of

nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $X$ be a four-dimensional manifold with boundary and let $W$ be a compact surface with boundary. An embedding $e:(W,\partial W)\to(X,\partial X)$ is proper when $e^{-1}(\partial X)=\partial W$. It is locally flat at an interior point of $W$ when there are neighborhoods of the point and its image and a homeomorphism of pairs from those neighborhoods to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$, with the standard linear plane $\mathbb R^2\subset\mathbb R^4$. It is locally flat at a boundary point when there are such neighborhoods and a homeomorphism of pairs to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$, where $\mathbb R^4_+=\{x_4\geq0\}$ and $\mathbb R^2_+=\{x_2=x_3=0,\ x_4\geq0\}$; the line $\partial\mathbb R^2_+$ lies in $\partial\mathbb R^4_+$. A collar of a boundary circle of $W$ is an embedding of that circle times $[0,\varepsilon)$ into $W$ that is the identity on the circle at parameter $0$; a concordance collar is required to agree with the corresponding product collar of the ambient end. A smooth proper surface has the analogous smooth charts and collars, which are also topological locally flat charts.

In ZF, let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth, and let $a\in U$. If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open neighbourhoods $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that $f|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Writing $g=(f|_V)^{-1}$,
$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$
No choice axiom is used.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Their compact track has a neighborhood with closure in the interior of $B^4$. By [F1] this isotopy extends ambiently in $\mathbb R^4$ with support in that neighborhood. Its time-one map fixes an ambient neighborhood of the outer boundary, preserves orientation and takes $p$ to $0$, while agreeing with translation on the whole ball $D$. Replace $F$ by its image. No conclusion about any nonround ball complement has been drawn.

**Flatten the surface on an actual neighborhood of zero.** Let $P$ be the tangent plane of the new surface at $0$. Orthogonal projection to $P$ has invertible derivative on that tangent plane, so [F3] writes the surface as $(u,h(u))$ in $P\oplus P^\perp$, with $h(0)=0$ and $Dh(0)=0$. Choose one sufficiently small closed disk in the $u$ coordinates. Its graph is a compact embedded disk in the interior of $B^4$. The maps $u\mapsto(u,(1-t)h(u))$ are an isotopy of that compact disk, since projection to $u$ remains injective with injective differential. Choose the disk small enough that its entire compact track lies in the interior of $B^4$. Apply [F1] again there, obtaining an ambient orientation-preserving diffeomorphism that fixes an ambient neighborhood of the outer boundary and maps the full graph disk to the flat disk. The surface is now exactly $P$ near $0$: the disk interior is an open neighborhood of $0$ within the embedded surface. Its complement outside a smaller such graph disk is compact and misses $0$, so it has positive distance from $0$. Choose $\varepsilon>0$ smaller than that distance and the flat disk radius, and less than $1$. Then the surface meets the actual round ball $B^4_\varepsilon$ precisely in $P\cap B^4_\varepsilon$. Compose the two ambient diffeomorphisms to obtain $\Psi$. They fix a common ambient neighborhood $N$ of the outer boundary. A finite cover of the compact circle by product neighborhoods gives one $0<\delta<\eta$ with $c(K\times[0,\delta])\subset N$. **Use only the concentric round shell.** The explicit map $(z,t)\mapsto(\varepsilon+(1-\varepsilon)t)z$ is a diffeomorphism $S^3\times[0,1]\to B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$. The inner boundary curve is the great circle $P\cap S^3_\varepsilon$, hence a standard unknot after radial rescaling; an orthonormal basis of $P$ extends by finite linear algebra to an oriented orthonormal basis of $\mathbb R^4$, giving an orientation-preserving linear rotation identifying it with the usual equator. Near the inner sphere the surface is a radial product in $P$, so this radial shell coordinate already supplies its product collar.

**Respect a restriction of the given outer surface collar.** For completeness the original outer surface collar need not be radial. In its smooth proper half-space chart the radial coordinate has nonzero inward derivative along a transverse collar direction. In a supplied parametrization of that collar, [F3] and compactness of its boundary circle therefore reparametrize it, for $r$ near $1$, as $(r f_r(\theta))$ with $f_r:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ a smooth embedding family and $f_1$ the original parametrized $K$. Thus adjust the shell identification by this map. It leaves the inner sphere and the boundary knot fixed, and changes neither genus nor the fixedness of a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar by $\Psi$ from steps 1.1–2.1. Reversing the interval and the surface orientation gives the reverse direction if desired; a half-turn reverses the orientation of the standard unknot. citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere,
$$
|s(K)|\le 2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K),
$$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surface in the standard four-ball with oriented boundary $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a connected compact oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with product collars and oriented boundary $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$ for oriented knots $K_0,K_1$ in the standard three-sphere. A **finite movie** for $S$ is a finite ordered sequence of regular-level link diagrams whose changes are planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves, births, saddles or deaths. Such a movie defines a map on rational Lee homology that preserves the induced decreasing filtration with degree $\chi(S)=-2g$. The map is an isomorphism; consequently
$$
|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le 2g.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil in the Hedden–Ording twist convention, with companion-annulus framing two. Equivalently, start with the three-crossing positive trefoil blackboard parallel, add one negative full annulus twist, and attach the positive clasp as in the admitted sixteen-crossing code. Then
$$s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

derivations.claim: Use the admitted cable/clasp diagram of [[lem-explicit-two-twisted-whitehead-double-has-sixteen-crossing-code]]. Its four-strand cable word is $\sigma_1^{-2}(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3\sigma_2)^3$, with the separate two-crossing clasp and the admitted wiring. The correction to blackboard framing is $-1$ full twist; the trefoil's blackboard framing is $+3$, giving exactly two full twists relative to the zero longitude. Here is a finite grid admission for this same diagram. Draw its sixteen crossing disks and joining orthogonal arrows, scale by $100$, and rotate the drawing by a quarter turn. At a horizontal overcrossing replace its overarc by the ordered vertices $(-10,0),(2,0),(2,4),(10,4),(10,0)$ and its underarc by $(0,-10),(4,-10),(4,2),(0,2),(0,10)$, reversing either order to retain its directed strand. The sole crossing is now $(2,2)$ with the same signed boundary ports. The six required replacements have disjoint supports. Delete straight subdivisions, separate coincident levels by perturbations smaller than $1/100$, and rank the levels. This gives a $33$-grid with exactly the sixteen original signed crossings. Its saved $986$ exchanges, cyclic cuts and three-corner destabilizations give the following $12$-grid, with zero-based rows: $$O=(4,9,6,1,2,11,0,8,5,3,7,10),\qquad X=(8,2,0,7,10,4,5,3,1,9,11,6).$$ Each exchange has nonalternating endpoint intervals or the permitted shared endpoint; each destabilization has three alternating marks in adjacent rows and columns. These conditions verify the individual isotopies and the displayed endpoint. The directed word is the negative reverse of the input traversal: the negative is the orientation-preserving change of viewing direction $(x,y,h)\mapsto(x,-y,-h)$, while the reverse records the independently chosen component orientation. Thus the actual grid is for the reverse of the oriented knot in the Statement, with its positive clasp and Hedden–Ording $t=2$ framing retained. The complete integer arrows and finite move list are recorded with the computation data below; neither a knot-table name nor a Floer rank identifies this knot.

The orientation junction preserves the normalized filtered invariant without an ambient invertibility assumption. For a doubly-pointed diagram of an oriented knot $J$, swapping only $w,z$ presents $J^r$. The actual disks are unchanged and their two marked degrees exchange, so $I:[x,i,j]\mapsto[x,j,i]$ is a Laurent-linear swap-filtered chain isomorphism to that diagram. The carried zero-Seifert cap gives $A'(x)=-A(x)$. The relative disk index then gives $M'(x)=M(x)-2A(x)+c$ for one integer $c$, so $I$ has constant full Maslov degree $c$. Compose it with the normalized same-oriented-knot conjugation of [F4], whose Maslov degree is zero and which swaps the two filtrations, including its inverse and homotopies. The composite is an ordinary bifiltered equivalence to $J^r$ of degree $c$. Its vertical hat quotient is an isomorphism between the two total three-sphere hat groups, each concentrated in normalized Maslov degree zero; hence $c=0$. This proves equality of the normalized inclusion thresholds for $J,J^r$. It also identifies their normalized bigraded knot Floer homologies. Apply this to the grid in step 1.1. Reflecting its columns, $O_r\mapsto11-O_r$ and $X_r\mapsto11-X_r$, gives a grid for its mirror: $(x,y,h)\mapsto(-x,y,h)$ reverses ambient orientation and keeps vertical strands over horizontal strands. No further knot-recognition premise is needed for this second grid.

Compute the multi-pointed hat filtered grid differential of each explicit grid: set every $O$-variable of the full minus grid complex to zero and retain every $O$-empty rectangle, including those containing $X$-markings. For a permutation state $p$, use $M_O(p)=I(p,p)-I(p,O)-I(O,p)+I(O,O)+1$ and $2A(p)=M_O(p)-M_X(p)-11$, with marks at half-integer cell centers and $I$ counting pairs strictly increasing in both coordinates. In the quotient $Q=C/F_0C$ retain exactly the states with $A>0$. Only Maslov degrees $-1,0,1$ enter $H_0(Q)$; discarding the outgoing differential from degree $-1$ does not change that group. The inventory is exhaustive by the following finite assignment recurrence. For used columns $S$ in the first $r=|S|$ rows, choosing $c\notin S$ increments the state-state term by $|\{b\in S:b<c\}|$. Add $-\#\{k\ge r:O_k\ge c\}-\#\{k<r:O_k<c\}$ to obtain the Maslov increment; the Alexander increment is the corresponding $X$ expression minus its $O$ expression. Accumulating the resulting two-variable polynomial over the $4096$ column subsets counts every permutation exactly once. For every retained state and ordered pair of distinct rows, take the corresponding oriented torus rectangle; the ordered pair includes both cyclic orientations, so complementary rectangles are counted in their respective directions. Reject a rectangle containing an interior state point or an $O$-marking, and retain every other rectangle, including those containing $X$-markings. Its output transposes the two chosen columns; discard that output only when its Alexander value is at most zero. Summing modulo two gives the actual quotient matrix. The first grid has $45\,824$ retained states, $159\,685$ rectangle orbits, including $24\,181$ with positive $X$ multiplicity, and $158\,523$ nonzero matrix entries. The reflected grid has $6080$ retained states and $11\,474$ rectangle orbits and nonzero entries. Every term has Maslov drop one and Alexander drop exactly its $X$ multiplicity; actual matrix multiplication gives $d^2=0$ in both quotients. These are the literal rectangle counts of [L1], rather than a formal-domain enumeration.

Exact column elimination over $\mathbb F_2$ gives $$\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}&\dim Q_1&\dim Q_0&\dim Q_{-1}&\operatorname{rank}d_1&\operatorname{rank}d_0\\\hline G&12347&17919&15558&8384&9535\\G^{\mathrm{mirror}}&4385&1463&232&1243&220.\end{array}$$ To specify the finite rank operation, encode a column by its row bits; repeatedly cancel its highest nonzero row with the previously retained pivot column at that row, or retain it as a new pivot if no such column exists. The counts of retained pivots are the displayed ranks. The saved complete columns and pivot-reduction traces give these computations directly. A separate exact verification used the complete joint assignment polynomial, checked every state and both normalized grid gradings, reconstructed every retained rectangle, checked $d^2$, and recomputed both ranks. Thus $$\dim H_0(Q_G)=17919-8384-9535=0,\qquad\dim H_0(Q_{G^{\mathrm{mirror}}})=1463-1243-220=0.$$ This uses the full filtered quotients, including the positive-$X$ terms in the first matrix.

Apply [L1]'s absolutely normalized filtered comparison and specialize all marking variables to zero. The multi-pointed hat filtered grid complex is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to the doubly-pointed full hat complex tensored with $V^{\otimes11}$, where the two degrees of $V$ are $(M,A)=(0,0),(-1,-1)$. Its total Maslov-zero homology is consequently one-dimensional, represented by the normalized three-sphere generator tensored with the sole degree-zero vector of $V^{\otimes11}$. Its filtration threshold is exactly $\tau(J)$: inclusion into that tensor factor and projection onto it are filtered degree-zero chain maps, so they give both threshold inequalities. The exact sequence $0\to F_0C\to C\to Q\to0$ and step 4.1 show that this total Maslov-zero class comes from $H_0(F_0C)$ for each grid. Hence $\tau(J)\le0$ and $\tau(mJ)\le0$, for the actual knot $J$ of step 1.1 and its mirror.

For completeness derive the required threshold sign from [F4]'s normalized reverse-mirror duality. Let $D$ be the finite normalized doubly-pointed full hat complex and write $t$ for its inclusion threshold. Its dual filtration is $F_sD^\vee=\{\lambda:\lambda(F_{-s-1}D)=0\}$. Choose a total generator cycle $z\in F_tD_0$. Then $z\notin\operatorname{im}(d:D_1\to D_0)+F_{t-1}D_0$: any such expression would give a homologous cycle at level $t-1$. Finite-dimensional linear algebra therefore gives a functional $\lambda$ vanishing on that sum and taking value one on $z$. It is a nonzero dual homology class at filtration $-t$. Conversely every functional at level $s<-t$ vanishes on $F_tD$, hence on $z$, and cannot represent the nonzero dual class. Thus the dual threshold is exactly $-t$. The absolute normalization and full duality in [F4], together with the orientation junction of step 2.1, give $\tau(mJ)=-\tau(J)$. Combining the two actual quotient inequalities of step 5.1 forces $\tau(J)=0$. By step 2.1 this is the normalized tau value of the actual positive Whitehead double with Hedden–Ording parameter $t=2$ in the Statement.

The admitted diagram and framing in step 1.1 are also those of [F3]. That accepted finite Lee computation gives $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$. Together with the independently established normalized value in step 6.1 this proves both numerical assertions of the Statement. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 6.1, algebra] ∎
